response.rationale: The MRI directly shows a filling defect in the common hepatic artery, indicating hepatic artery thrombosis. The bile duct dilation and left lobe atrophy are downstream ischemic consequences of impaired arterial supply to the biliary tree and liver.

rejected.why: Explains the renal presentation and CT renal findings but not the hepatic artery filling defect or biliary/lobar changes.
Too nonspecific; the imaging evidence localizes the thrombotic process to the hepatic artery.
Describes a biliary imaging finding rather than the underlying arterial cause.
Duplicate of the bile duct dilation finding and does not address the arterial filling defect.
Budd-Chiari syndrome involves hepatic venous outflow obstruction, not an arterial filling defect.
